title: Codec Gate Predicate
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $n,s\in\mathbb{N}$, and choose codec positions, a codec case, an encoded bit, and a Boolean assignment to the codec ports. The gate is true exactly when either the assignment does not satisfy the codec guard for these data, or its new-bit value equals the expected value of the chosen encoded bit under the action determined by the codec case.
hypotheses_covered: Finite Turing machine with Boolean alphabet
A Boolean assignment to the codec ports
caveat: The supplied snippet does not include the definitions of the codec guard, codec action, or expected-bit function, so their detailed meanings cannot be stated from the given ground truth.
